land.text: the Lower Don and the Don-Volga steppe, the Host's land

successors.note: Not a conquest: the Cossacks page calls the Host 'an autonomous military state formation of the Don Cossacks under the citizenship of the Moscow State' and 'autonomous ... in 1671-1786', undated before that. The end year is Cliopatria's 1641 plus the year of the Azov withdrawal; no page opened dates the absorption (see notes).

capitals.name: Cherkassk (Starocherkassk)
capitals.note: Page: the fortress 'was probably built before 1570 although it is first mentioned in chronicles from 1593. After fifty years it became the capital of the Don Cossacks' (about the 1640s). Razdory, the earlier seat, is not on any page opened; 1593 is the first mention, used as a stand-in. Coordinates approximate.

correction.text: the 1552 shape unchanged; it also holds for 1549-1551 (first records of the stanitsas)

keyframe_review.note: 64.4 k km2 on the Lower Don (bbox 38.4-43.3E, 47.1-49.8N). The page dates the first records of the Cossack villages to 1549 ('The first records relating to the Cossack villages: the stanitsas, date back to 1549'), three years before Cliopatria's first shape; in 1552 Ataman Susar Fedorov joined Ivan IV's army. The only area figure on any page opened is the later Don Host Oblast (162,889 km2, 1870-1920): 64 k is 0.4 of it, beyond the factor of two, but the oblast is a different, later territory and the page is silent on the early extent, so the shape stands. The shape does not include Azov (gazetteer).

64.3 k km2, unchanged but for one cell. Nothing on the pages opened dates a change in 1595. Cossacks page: under Boris Godunov the Don Cossacks were ordered 'to drive away from the Don all the Ukrainian Cossacks' (1590s).

126.0 k km2: +61.7 k km2 in the Don-Volga steppe and the Khoper-Medveditsa country (bbox 41.0-45.2E, 48.2-51.6N). No page opened dates or describes this enlargement (the Don Host Oblast and Starocherkasskaya pages say nothing of the 17th-century extent); kept as drawn (unverified: no page). Infobox comparison as for the first shape: 126 k against the later oblast's 163 k is 0.78.
126.4 k km2, one cell more than 1636. Azov (39.4E, 47.1N), held 1637-1642, lies outside the shape, so the ledger carries it as an occupation of Ottoman land.

correction.text: the 1641 shape unchanged for the year of the Azov withdrawal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends 1641, but the tsar ordered the Cossacks to evacuate Azov in March 1642 and the Ottomans reoccupied it in September 1642; the Host's last year in this dossier. After 1642 the Host's land is inside no Tsardom shape (see notes).

region.text: the Cossack villages (stanitsas) on the Lower Don

ledger.note: 1549: the first records of the Don Cossack stanitsas. 'The first records relating to the Cossack villages: the stanitsas, date back to 1549.' The page adds that the steppe of the Don region had been populated 'since the 14th century' and that after the Golden Horde's fall (1480) the Don area was divided between the Crimean west side and the Nogai east side; no Host of record before the 1549 villages.

region.text: the Ottoman fortress of Azov at the mouth of the Don

ledger.note: 1637: the Don Cossacks storm Azov. 'On 18 June Tatarinov's forces breached most of Azov's outer defenses' after a mine, and the Ottoman garrison 'had to capitulate three days later'; the Zaporozhian Cossacks joined them (Don Cossacks page). On 15 July they sent a delegation to Moscow asking Tsar Mikhail to take Azov under his protection; Moscow disowned them.

region.text: the Host's land on the Lower Don and in the Don-Volga steppe

ledger.note: 1642: the Don Host leaves the map as a state (Cliopatria's row ends 1641). The page is silent on any act of absorption: the Cossacks page calls the Host 'an autonomous military state formation of the Don Cossacks under the citizenship of the Moscow State' and dates autonomy '1671-1786'; the Starocherkasskaya page has the Cossacks first 'an independent entity in between Russia, Turkey and Poland' and 'later a vassal of the Russian tzars'. Bridging year, not a dated event: a gap-filler should continue the Host as the tsar's client.

1642: the Cossacks evacuate Azov. 'When Sultan Ibrahim issued a new ultimatum to Moscow on March 1642, Tsar Mikhail complied and ordered the Don Cossacks to evacuate Azov'; the infobox date range ends 30 April 1642 and 'Ottoman forces reoccupied Azov in September 1642'. The 1641 siege (Hüseyin Pasha reached Azov on 7 June 1641; the Ottoman council met again on 20 September) was lifted without result.

wars.name: Russo-Kazan Wars
wars.outcome: Kazan fell on 2 October 1552; 'In the year 1552 Don Cossacks under the command of Ataman Susar Fedorov joined the Army of Ivan the Terrible'. No Don land changed.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Astrakhan
wars.outcome: 'On 2 June 1556 the Cossack regiment of Ataman Lyapun Filimonov ... conquered and annexed the Astrakhan Khanate' for Moscow; the Host gained no land.

wars.name: Siege of Azov (1637-1642)
wars.outcome: Don and Zaporozhian Cossacks took Azov in June 1637 and held it 'for the next five years'; the Ottoman-Tatar army besieged it from 7 June 1641 without success; Moscow, having disowned the Cossacks, ordered the evacuation in March 1642 and the Ottomans reoccupied Azov in September 1642. Infobox: Ottoman victory.

certainty.note: A steppe and river frontier with no survey or treaty line; the Host's extent is Cliopatria's and no page opened describes it. Azov (1637-1642) is a fortress, not a frontier.

notes:
Written 2026-10-31 by the eu-16-h agent from 5 pages (the budget).

Cliopatria row: 'Don Cossacks', 1552..1641, 4 shapes of 64-126 k km2 on the Lower Don. The state is dated 1549 (first records of the stanitsas) to 1642 (the Azov withdrawal): both ends are weak. The pages give no founding of the Host ('from the end of the 16th century until 1918'), no oath to the tsar and no capital dates; 'Razdory' is on none of them. The 1549 start is the first documented record of villages, confidence 2.

The hole after 1641 (important). Cliopatria's Don row stops in 1641, and no Tsardom of Russia shape from 1642 to 1720 contains the Don land (the gazetteer finds 0 cells of Rostov oblast in any of them); the Russian Empire shape from 1721 has to be checked by the gap-filler. The Cossacks page calls the Host 'an autonomous military state formation of the Don Cossacks under the citizenship of the Moscow State' and gives 1671-1786 for its autonomy, and the Don Cossacks page keeps the Host alive to 1918 (Don Host Land from 1786, Don Host Oblast 1870-1920). The dossier therefore ends at 1642 only because Cliopatria does; the 'dissolve' event is a bridging judgment (confidence 1, page silent) and the real continuation (a client of the Tsardom drawn in the lighter tint, 1643-1786 or later) needs a dossier extension or a vassal event in the Tsardom's, with a source for the dates. The Tsardom dossier records the hole in its notes and does not write a vassal event for it.

Unverified: the 1636 enlargement (+61.7 k km2 between the Don and the Volga); the early extent (no page); the capital before the 1640s.

Counterparts: Ottoman Empire (Azov occupation, 1637-1642; the Ottoman dossier should carry the matching loss and gain), Zaporozhian Cossacks (joined the capture of Azov 1637 on the Cossacks and Don Cossacks pages), Crimean Khanate (joined the 1641 siege), Nogai Horde and Crimean Khanate (the divided Don area after 1480: no event, the shape is Cossack from 1552), Kalmyk Khanate (the seed lists it as a neighbour from 1636; no page opened).
